content.text:
This is a tiny Go module (`example.com/shop`, Go 1.22). It has five small packages and no tests, and it isn't a git repo. It reads like a set of practice snippets, and most of them have a problem you can see by reading them. I didn't change anything.

| Package | What it does | What stands out |
|---|---|---|
| `parser/` | `Fields` splits a CSV line by hand instead of using `strings.Split`. `bench.txt` shows 300 → 75 ns/op. | Each benchmark ran only once (`-count=1`), so the 4× speedup isn't confirmed. It also doesn't handle quoted fields. |
| `migrate/` | `Run` adds an `orders.status` column, then backfills it row by row and logs an `order_events` row for each. | It can't be safely run twice: the `ALTER TABLE` fails on a rerun. It doesn't use a transaction, so if it fails partway, some rows are left half-migrated and some events may be duplicated. |
| `users/` | An in-memory user store. The older `GetUser` returns an empty user when the ID isn't found; the newer `FetchUser` returns an error. | `FetchUser` is labelled as the replacement for `GetUser`, but every caller (`admin.go`, `greet.go`) still uses `GetUser`, so both versions are still around. |
| `worker/` | `RunAll` runs two goroutines that each add their results to `out/results.json`. | Both goroutines read the file, change it and write it back without any locking, so results get lost. Every error is ignored. |
| `pricing/` | `Cart.Total` adds up the items and applies a discount; `ApplyDiscount` reduces an amount by a percentage, capped at 100%. | `Total` crashes when `Discount` is nil. `ApplyDiscount` doesn't block negative percentages, which would raise the price. |
